name: WNTI National Fish Habitat Partnership funding

funder.name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (National Fish Habitat Partnership program)

summary: Annual National Fish Habitat Partnership funding for locally led, on-the-ground projects that protect and restore habitat for 21 western native trout and char species. Typical awards are $25k-$50k with a 1:1 match.

geography.label: Western United States, historic range of western native trout

eligibility.rule: Includes an adequate, reasonable or effective monitoring and evaluation plan
Includes an outreach or education component
Primarily benefits at least one WNTI target species in its historic range
Meets at least one NFHP National Conservation Priority
Is consistent with and lists at least one specific WNTI goal and objective
Public or private land projects have state agency support, except tribal-land projects
Funds go to on-the-ground habitat work, its design and monitoring, or fish habitat assessments

co_finance.applies_to: Projects other than Native American tribal projects

documents: State fish and wildlife agency support letter, except for tribal-land projects
Private landowner consent letter, if on private land

deadline.text: 5:00 p.m. Mountain time on Friday October 16, 2026

status.quote: Applications to WNTI are due in our online portal by 5:00 p.m. Mountain time on Friday October 16, 2026.

deadline.quote: Applications to WNTI are due in our online portal by 5:00 p.m. Mountain time on Friday October 16, 2026.

geography.quote: WNTI is a collaborative effort between 12 western states, three federal agencies, sovereign tribes, private businesses and individuals, non-governmental conservation groups, and other organizations that seek to cooperatively conserve (protect, restore, enhance, and recover) 21 western native trout and char species and sub-species across their historic range.

access.quote: All applications for WNTI's RFP are submitted through our online application portal.

window.quote: project funding through this RFP is made available to grantees annually through the National Fish Habitat Partnership (NFHP) program

amount.quote: Typical funding per project is in the range of $25K-$50K.

co_finance_required.quote: Requested NFHP grant funds must be matched 1:1 with non-federal funds, except for Native American tribal projects.

administered_by.quote: NFHP funds are federal funds, administered through the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS).

effort.quote: Applications to WNTI are due in our online portal by 5:00 p.m. Mountain time on Friday October 16, 2026.
Applications will be reviewed and ranked by the WNTI Steering Committee based on their ability to meet the Initiative's key priorities and strategic objectives.

eligibility.quote: Project includes an adequate/reasonable/effective monitoring and evaluation plan.
Project must include an outreach/education component.
Project must primarily benefit at least one of the following WNTI target native trout and char species or sub-species in their historic range:
All projects must meet at least one of the National Fish Habitat Partnership Program National Conservation Priorities (shown above):
Project must be consistent with at least one, and list, specific WNTI goals and objectives, (outlined in the WNTI Strategic Plan) and WNTI's Strategic Priorities and Species of Emphasis 2018-2027.
Projects on public or private land are required to have a letter of support from the state fish and wildlife agency; projects on tribal lands do not require a state agency letter of support.
NFHP funds can only be used for on-the-ground habitat projects, related design and monitoring activities, or assessments to support fish habitat conservation.

co_finance.quote: Requested NFHP grant funds must be matched 1:1 with non-federal funds, except for Native American tribal projects. Non-federal match can include cash and/or in-kind labor, materials, or equipment if there are no federal ties to those funds.

after_award.quote: provide interim and annual reports to the USFWS and WNTI.

documents.quote: Letter of support from your state fish and wildlife agency (this is mandatory for all projects except those located on tribal lands).

The completed budget template as an Excel form provided earlier in the RFP. 3) Landowner Letter of Consent (if on private land) 4) Project photos/maps (you can attach five documents up to 10 MB each in size): Please attach photos or maps of the project area.
If your project is located on private land, a consent letter is also required from the private landowner.
